title_original: Fremantle’s Andrea Scrosati to leave to set up new venture
excerpt_original: Group’s COO was a key architect of its film investment strategy.

blocks.text: Fremantle COO Andrea Scrosati, a key architect of its film investment strategy, is leaving the production and distribution group after eight years.
Scrosati plans to launch a new entrepreneurial venture and will remain with the company until the end of January 2027 to support the transition.
Scrosati joined London-based Fremantle as group COO in November 2018 from Sky Italia, adding responsibility as CEO for Continental Europe in 2021.
He led the group’s M&A strategy, overseeing the acquisition of a number of leading independent production companies and labels including Element Pictures, Asacha Media Group and Lux Vide.

Scrosati was also instrumental in developing Fremantle’s global film strategy, helping the company deliver its 100 th film in 2026. Films produced by Fremantle labels in recent years include Bugonia , Maria , Pillion , Poor Things , The Hand Of God , There’s Still Tomorrow , My Father’s Shadow , The Chronology Of Water , La Grazia and On Becoming A Guinea Fowl.
Earlier this year, Fremantle announced that it was moving away from fully financing feature films following a strategic review by parent company RTL Group.

links.text: moving away from fully financing feature films

blocks.text: Fremantle’s focus on film is widely viewed to have paid off in terms of securing prestigious festival berths and critical acclaim, but box-office results have been more mixed.
Scrosati also spearheaded the creation of Imaginae Studios, the company’s standalone AI-focused production label.

Jennifer Mullin, Global CEO Fremantle, said: “Andrea has made an enormous contribution to Fremantle over the past eight years. He has been instrumental in our growth and transformation, from helping build Fremantle into a true portfolio company and leading our M&A strategy, to establishing our film strategy and constantly pushing us to think differently about innovation and the future of our business.”

Scrosati said: “These eight years at Fremantle have been an extraordinary privilege. Fremantle is a unique company, with incredible people, some of the world’s finest creative talent and an exceptional portfolio of IP. I leave with enormous pride in what we have achieved together and great affection for the company and everyone who makes it what it is. The time feels right for me to take the next step and focus on building something new.”
